key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can efficiently map the thermodynamic stability of complex hybrid perovskite alloys across composition and phase space.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies composition windows that are most likely to yield stable, tunable solar-cell materials, with especially narrower stable regions for Sn-based alloys than Pb-based ones.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data for fast structure relaxation.
Secondary ML models predict energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
Free-energy landscapes are computed across (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3 while accounting for disorder and FA orientations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports free-energy calculations across compositions and phases, showing maximum stability at high iodide content and no stabilization near the center of composition space.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on ML models trained on DFT data, accuracy may degrade outside the sampled composition/structure domain.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
